parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-11, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 82.6 | 5.04 | 5.04
2 | 162.4 | 1.62 | 6.66
3 | 121.3 | 2.57 | 9.23
4 | 152.0 | 0.91 | 10.14
5 | 105.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-11, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**VES Station T-11 Site Report**

**Location:** Survey Area T  
**Model Summary:**  
A 5-layer geoelectric profile is delineated to a depth beyond 10.14 m:
- **Layer 1:** 82.6 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 5.04 m (depth to base: 5.04 m)
- **Layer 2:** 162.4 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 1.62 m (depth to base: 6.66 m)
- **Layer 3:** 121.3 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 2.57 m (depth to base: 9.23 m)
- **Layer 4:** 152.0 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 0.91 m (depth to base: 10.14 m)
- **Layer 5:** 105.9 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (basement/underlying unit)

**Curve Evaluation:**  
Analyzing the consecutive 3-layer segments yields:
- Layers 1–3 ($82.6 < 162.4 > 121.3$): **K-type**
- Layers 2–4 ($162.4 > 121.3 < 152.0$): **H-type**
- Layers 3–5 ($121.3 < 152.0 > 105.9$): **K-type**

The resulting sequence matches the on-file **KHK-type** classification.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
